title: SPARC - Analysis of multiplexed bead data using MPLEX software
author: J Paul Robinson
materials: This directory must be available to the MPLEX software. The MPLEX software requires a license file to be placed in the same directory as the EXE file before the software will operate. The software is only available to academic and non-profit institutions.
Select a protocol from the OPtions Menu (optionsMPLEX.giif)

steps.title: Prepare and Organize Data Files
steps.instruction: Transfer flow cytometer data files to the appropriate computer directory, ensuring all files are in the same directory and in FCS format.

substeps.instruction: Verify that each file is properly identified by the row and column ID of the 96 or 384 well plate (e.g., A1, B2, F12) within the filename.

steps.title: Load Data into MPLEX
steps.instruction: Launch the MPLEX software and import the data files.

substeps.instruction: Select the LOAD ICON in the top left corner.
Select the directory containing the FCS data files to load them.

steps.title: Assign Gates to Light Scatter
steps.instruction: Identify and assign bead populations using the light scatter data, ignoring 'satellite' beads (doublets) that form small, non-key populations.

substeps.instruction: Use the SEMIAutomatic function to create gate regions.
Adjust the scroll bar on the right to display the exact number of bead populations selected (e.g., 10 populations for a 10-bead set).
Select the 'CREATE GATES' button on the top left.

steps.title: Verify and Reassign Bead Populations
steps.instruction: Review the applied bead gates against the manufacturer's bead map to ensure correct placement.

substeps.instruction: Identify any incorrectly placed bead populations.
Reassign populations by clicking the correct bead number from the assay list on the left and dragging it to the correct gate on the scatter plot.

steps.title: Lock Assay Design
steps.instruction: Save the bead assignments and assay design for the data set.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Set As Default' on the top right to lock in the assignments.
Verify that the final analysis screen shows bead populations matching the manufacturer map and that standard curves appear correctly.

steps.title: Configure Plate Map
steps.instruction: Create and associate a plate map to designate sample identities.

substeps.instruction: Run the PLATE MAP protocol to create a map.
Select the plate map ICON to open the map.
Ensure the plate name mirrors the data set directory name (e.g., 'r1012-TEST SET FOR DEMO').

steps.title: Export Data
steps.instruction: Output the analyzed data using one of the two available methods based on the required format.

substeps.instruction: Select 'To CSV' for a standard comma-separated values file.
Select the 'NIH' button to create NIH SPARC program required directories and file structures, including 'derivative', 'primary', and 'source' folders containing data and metadata.
